injury.comment: Wright carried the ball five times for 10 yards and returned three kickoffs for 79 yards during Miami's loss to the Bills on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Wright continues to struggle rushing the ball this season, averaging just 1.6 yards per carry across 30 rush attempts. The 23-year-old will look to improve upon his performance during the Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.

injury.comment: Worthy caught two of four targets for 38 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals.
injury.longComment: Worthy was able to eclipse 30 receiving yards for just the second time in the last five weeks, but it was a step in the right direction after being blanked on three targets in Week 10. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he connected with quarterback Patrick Mahomes for an 18-yard touchdown. The score was Worthy's second of the year and first since Week 2, and his next chance to build off of Sunday's performance will come on Thanksgiving against the Bills.

injury.comment: Cooper caught four of his five targets for 59 yards in the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Cooper played 46 offensive snaps and 15 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver continues to play most of the offensive snaps for the Eagles, seeing two more targets than rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon in the Week 11 win.

injury.comment: Strange caught all three of his targets for 16 yards during Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: Strange was able to notch at least three catches for the first time since Week 6, but he still finished with fewer than 20 receiving yards for the second straight week and third time overall this year. The tight end has now reeled in 35 of 43 targets for 381 yards and two touchdowns over 10 contests during the 2026 season.

injury.comment: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as Chicago's emergency third quarterback Sunday versus the Saints.
injury.longComment: It's the fifth straight week that Keenum will work as the Bears' emergency third quarterback. That means he can enter Sunday's contest only if both Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Broncos' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As the emergency QB3, Ehlinger is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback against the Cardinals on Sunday.
injury.longComment: The rookie seventh-rounder has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026. As the emergency QB3, Nussmeier is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that, at this time, surgery to address Willis' groin/core injury is not foreseen, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
injury.longComment: That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.

injury.comment: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Bears on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As the emergency QB3, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless starter Tyler Shough and backup Spencer Rattler both leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection. Wilson has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026.

injury.comment: Knee - Meniscus
Payton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Steelers on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As the emergency third quarterback, Payton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Calf
Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. he added five yards on two carries.
injury.longComment: The 40-year-old QB was pressed into duty with rookie Carson Beck (back) on the shelf, and Johnson unsurprisingly wasn't really up to the task after the Cardinals fell into a 14-0 hole before the first quarter was over. Johnson spent most of his afternoon finding Trey McBride for short gains, and he did hit Simi Fehoko for a two-yard score in the second quarter. Beck doesn't figure to miss much time, but if Johnson gets another start in Week 12, he'll be taking on a much less formidable Commanders defense.

injury.comment: Elbow
Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency quarterback against the Eagles on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As has been the case all year, Howard will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph. As such, Howard is not allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Rodgers and Rudolph leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Groin
Stick (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Lions, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
injury.longComment: The Buccaneers elevated Stick from the team's practice squad Monday. The 31-year-old will only be eligible to play should both Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels exit with an injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: King (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Ravens on Sunday, Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.
injury.longComment: King will only play Sunday if both Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injury.comment: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers but will serve as the Ravens' emergency quarterback.
injury.longComment: Slovis will be inactive once again. However, if Jacoby Brissett and Joe Fagnano exit Sunday's meeting with Carolina due to an injury, illness or ejection, Slovis will be available to play.

injury.comment: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
injury.longComment: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

Ahmed saw action late in the third quarter and into the fourth, after Roschon Johnson exited the game with an ankle injury in the first quarter. Both are behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai on the depth chart.

injury.longComment: Corbin was elevated to the active roster for the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday. He finished that contest with five carries for 32 yards and one catch (on as many targets) for five yards, and those touches were spread across four quarters while he operated Javonte Williams' backup. With Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) both on injured reserve, Corbin is a top candidate to be elevated for Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

injury.longComment: Saylors didn't record any stats over two snaps on offense while he notched 29 yards on his only kick return of the day in Week 11. The running back will continue to be unintriguing fantasy option while operating as an extreme depth option behind Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit's backfield moving forward.

injury.longComment: Ott logged 12 offensive snaps and eight special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The running back saw a few carries behind Emmett Johnson due to the absence of Kenneth Walker (groin). With Walker likely returning for Thursday night against the Bills, Ott will likely return to seeing no offensive snaps.

injury.comment: VanSumeren (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
injury.longComment: VanSumeran injured his knee in the second half, and with no other fullback on the 53-man roster, the Chiefs could turn to tight end Jake Briningstool to provide additional blocking out of the backfield. VanSumeran's status over the coming days will be worth monitoring, given that the Chiefs are operating on a short week and play against the Bills on Thanksgiving Day.

injury.comment: Allen logged 80 kick return yards in the Dolphins' 26-9 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Allen played 16 special-teams snaps in the contest. The running back did not log an offensive snap, leaving all the rushing work to Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright.

injury.comment: Knee - ACL
Donaldson logged a five-yard carry and brought in all four of his targets for 12 yards during the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
injury.longComment: Donaldson recorded season highs in both catches and targets, and he finished third on the Saints in both of those categories behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. However, Donaldson coughed up the football on his first catch of the game early in the second quarter, which the Bears offense capitalized on with a six-play drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass from Caleb Williams to D'Andre Swift. Donaldson's 32 offensive snaps were tied with Travis Etienne for most among Saints running backs Sunday, although Etienne saw a heavier workload with 14 carries for 76 yards while Alvin Kamara, who played only eight offensive snaps, found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough in the second quarter. Losers of three of their last four games, the Saints will look to reverse their fortunes in Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injury.longComment: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

injury.comment: Davis didn't play an offensive snap in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
injury.longComment: As has been the case for three straight weeks, with Breece Hall back healthy, Davis has been glued to special teams for the Jets. He has no fantasy appeal.

injury.comment: Coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that the Cardinals are still evaluating the status of Love (ankle), with the running back's earliest possible return from IR on the horizon, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
injury.longComment: "I'll know a little bit more as this week goes," LaFleur noted of Love, who will miss at least one more game before potentially being activated ahead of, and available for, Week 13 action. Love sustained a right high-ankle sprain Nov. 1, and at the time he was thought to be facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. However, for this coming weekend's game against the Commanders at least, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will continue to handle Arizona's backfield duties.

injury.comment: Knee
Tucker didn't record any stats during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injury.longComment: Tucker didn't garner any touches on offense for the third straight week as Tampa Bay opted to use Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell exclusively in the backfield. Tucker will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as both Irving and Gainwell are available for the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Etienne rushed six times for 29 yards, caught one pass for seven yards, logged 36 kick return yards and eight punt return yards in the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Etienne did it all in Week 11 while only playing 10 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps. Despite the low snap counts, the running back influenced many areas of the box score. Etienne continues to be the reserve option behind bell-cow back Chuba Hubbard, who continues to amass carries and touchdowns for the Panthers offense.

injury.comment: Allen caught one pass for minus-1 yard in the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Allen played 14 offensive snaps behind Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and Chris Rodriguez, and Tuten ended up aggravating his ankle issue in the defeat. If Tuten needs to miss time, Allen could see elevated snaps behind Rodriguez, though Ameer Abdullah also is an option for the Jaguars out of the backfield. Ultimately, Allen is much likelier than not to remain irrelevant in fantasy.

injury.comment: Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
injury.longComment: For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.

injury.comment: Randall (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina.
injury.longComment: Randall was recently reinstated from injured reserve. However, with Derrick Henry, Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali available versus the Panthers, Randall will be inactive.

injury.comment: Ridley caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injury.longComment: Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

injury.comment: Harris caught both his targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
injury.longComment: With Ladd McConkey back in the lineup, Harris' role in the passing attack shrank after he'd turned 12 targets over the prior two games into an 8-92-0 line. Harris' fantasy appeal would collapse even further if Justin Herbert (concussion) ends up missing any time. The second-year wideout will at least get a promising matchup in Week 12 against a vulnerable Patriots secondary.

injury.comment: Franklin did not record a catch in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
injury.longComment: The wide receiver did see two targets, but he wasn't able to haul them in. Franklin has just 17 targets across 10 games this year, making nine catches for 100 yards and no scores.

injury.comment: Wilson caught three of six targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
injury.longComment: It was Wilson's first game since suffering a finger injury in Week 5 that landed him on injured reserve. He ended up playing 49 of 71 offensive snaps, 39 of which came out wide with 10 in the slot. Wilson had primarily operated as the Steelers' slot receiver prior to his injury, but Germie Bernard has emerged in that role for Pittsburgh. While Michael Pittman (foot) is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, DK Metcalf might receive some form of team-imposed discipline after he had an on-field meltdown against the Eagles before being ejected from the game.

injury.comment: Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
injury.longComment: Freiermuth matched his season high in catches, securing five passes in a game for the third time this year. The tight end has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards in a contest this season, and he entered Week 11 with exactly two catches in each of the team's last four games. Freiermuth has now caught 32 of 43 targets for 309 yards and five touchdowns while also adding four rushes for five yards and a score over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

injury.comment: Raymond caught one of four passes for 14 yards during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
injury.longComment: Raymond's four targets were tied with Rome Odunze for most on the Bears on Sunday, although the former could only muster a 14-yard grab early in the second quarter. Raymond has commanded four targets or more in six of 10 regular-season games and is up to a 33-304-1 receiving line on 45 targets while operating as Chicago's WR3 behind Odunze and Luther Burden. The Bears will hit the road to face the Lions on Thanksgiving Day.

Saints head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that Johnson is still undergoing further medical evaluation after injuring his hamstring during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
injury.longComment: The Saints expect to have a better feel for Johnson's status Wednesday, when the team holds its first practice of Week 12. Before exiting Sunday in the third quarter, Johnson was targeted just once and failed to record a reception for the second time in 10 appearances on the season. If the hamstring injury prevents Johnson from playing next weekend in Cincinnati, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be in line for added snaps at tight end.

injury.comment: Ayomanor caught all three of his targets for 27 yards in Sunday's loss to Dallas.
injury.longComment: Ayomanor logged season highs with five catches, 10 targets and 79 yards against Jacksonville in Week 10, but he reverted back closer to his usual numbers versus the Cowboys. The second-year wideout did rank third on the team in receptions and receiving yards, and his 37 offensive snaps were also third behind Carnell Tate (62) and Chimere Dike (54). Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season, but Ayomanor may be hard-pressed to put up reliable fantasy production as the third pass-catching option, at best, for one of the league's least prolific air attacks.

injury.comment: Fields caught two of his five targets for 25 yards in the Giants' 23-15 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Fields played 56 offensive snaps in the contest, logging 86 percent of the Giants' offensive plays. Despite the lack of catches, the No. 2 wide receiver continues to receive attention from quarterback J.J. McCarthy on a week-to-week basis.

injury.comment: Cameron caught three of seven targets for 44 yards during Sunday's 23-18 loss against the Giants. He also returned two kickoffs for a total of 40 return yards.
injury.longComment: Despite only being on the field for 25 of the Jaguars' 68 offensive snaps in Week 11, Cameron drew a career-high seven targets. He wasn't terribly efficient on those targets, but neither was Jacksonville's offense as a whole Sunday. He'll be lining up against a much softer pass defense in a Week 12 tilt versus the Titans.

injury.comment: Thomas caught one pass for an 18-yard touchdown on three targets in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: Thomas' three targets were a distant fourth on the team, as Parker Washington (17), Jakobi Meyers (10) and Josh Cameron (seven) combined to see a combined 34 looks on Trevor Lawrence's 47 pass attempts. Thomas ran 32 routes, 14 more than Cameron as the Jaguars' nominal WR3, but the former hasn't been seeing meaningful target volume for months. After drawing nine targets in Week 2, Thomas has averaged 2.1 targets per game over his last eight contests. He's well off the fantasy radar while Washington and Meyers are healthy.

injury.comment: Ferguson (knee/ankle) was listed as a non-participant on Monday's practice estimate, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
injury.longComment: While Ferguson was present for Monday's walkthrough, per Todd Archer of ESPN, he'll officially log a 'DNP' listing for the session, as the Cowboys prepare for Thursday afternoon's game against the Eagles. Ferguson, who has missed two straight contests, had been deemed a non-participant on practice reports over the past two weeks, with Monday's 'DNP' now giving the tight end two more chances to upgrade his listed participation level ahead of Week 12 action.

injury.comment: Dike caught six of seven targets for 69 yards during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injury.longComment: Dike was able to reel in multiple passes for the third straight game, and his six snags set a new season high for the second-year pro. The 24-year-old paced the team in targets Sunday, narrowly edging out fellow wide receivers Calvin Ridley (six) and Carnell Tate (five). Dike will have a chance to continue carving out a more substantial role for himself on offense moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign.

injury.comment: Virgil wasn't targeted in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injury.longComment: The 22-year-old wide receiver played just two offensive snaps, the same amount as Devin Duvernay, as the duo played behind all three of Simi Fehoko (52 snaps), Harrison Wallace (36) and Zay Jones (32) in the Cardinals' injury-ravaged wideout depth chart. Virgil has three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets across seven games this season. He's never been relevant in fantasy.

injury.comment: Andrews caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina.
injury.longComment: While the veteran tight end showed some instant chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett last week, Andrews saw his target volume crater in their second game together, as rookie depth TEs Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner saw similar usage as pass catchers. Andrews has failed to reach 25 receiving yards in five of his last six games and hasn't scored a TD in seven straight contests, making him a very risky fantasy option in Week 12 against the Texans.

injury.comment: Lane didn't garner a target during Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: Lane failed to reel in a pass for the second time in three weeks, and both times the ball was thrown his way Sunday, the play was negated by a defensive penalty, resulting in no targets for the rookie. Lane was on the field for 33 offensive snaps, ranking third at wide receiver for Baltimore behind Rashod Bateman (59) and Zay Flowers (57). Lane's next chance to get back on track will come in Week 12 against the Texans.

injury.comment: Legette did not play an offensive snap in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
injury.longComment: The wide receiver did play nine snaps on special teams. Legette missed six games with a knee injury before returning for Carolina's win over the Saints in Week 10, though he only saw action on two offensive snaps in that contest. Legette has two catches for 64 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season.

injury.comment: Washington caught all three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
injury.longComment: The big tight end earned just a 6.8 percent target share on a day when Aaron Rodgers fired off 44 pass attempts in prolonged comeback mode. Washington has been held to 25 yards or fewer in eight of 10 games this season. He doesn't see enough volume to warrant weekly fantasy consideration as a touchdown-or-bust bet.

injury.comment: Waller caught all three of his targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
injury.longComment: The veteran tight end was out-produced by second-year player Mitchell Evans, who posted a 5-44-1 line on five targets, but Waller made more of an impact than Tommy Tremble, who caught his only target for 18 yards. With all three members of the trio capable of making a splash in any given week, Waller will be tough to rely on heading into a Week 12 meeting with the Buccaneers.

injury.comment: Mooney did not catch any of his five targets during Sunday's 23-18 win versus the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: Quarterback J.J. McCarthy was inefficient against a solid Jaguars defense in Week 11, completing just 18 of his 38 pass attempts for 173 yards. A couple of those 20 incompletions were intended for an open Mooney, who continued to operate in the deeper areas of the field. He'll keep hunting for a big play in Week 12 at Indianapolis.

injury.comment: Johnson caught two of three targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injury.longComment: After being benched in the Bucs' pre-Week 9 bye loss to the Bears, ted Hurst was back in the good graces of the coaching staff and played ahead of Johnson as the WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin. That left Johnson as the fourth receiver, playing just 20 of 69 offensive snaps. He has 13 catches for 271 yards and one touchdown on 23 targets across 10 games this season.

injury.comment: Metchie caught one of three targets for 19 yards during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Metchie and Bryce Young connected on a 19-yard pass late in the third quarter to set the Panthers up in the red zone, and the drive ended four plays later on a 33-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. Metchie has caught one pass in each of his last two outings, and the fifth-year pro is firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker on the wide receiver depth chart. The Panthers will hit the road in Week 12 for a crucial NFC South clash against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.

injury.comment: Hunter caught his lone target for three yards, added a nine-yard carry and logged six tackles (four solo) during the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
injury.longComment: As has been the case for most of the 2026 season, Hunter spent the majority of his time on the field playing defense, and his six tackles were fourth-most on the Jaguars. He had a quiet day offensively, and the second-year pro is up to a 10-94-1 receiving line on 11 targets through 10 regular-season games. On the defensive side of the ball, Hunter is up to 42 tackles (28 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions).

injury.comment: Otton caught one pass for eight yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
injury.longComment: The tight end earned just a 9.1 percent target share and continues to be nearly invisible in the box score despite being an every-down player who runs virtually every pass route for the Bucs. Otton has just one touchdown since Week 11 of the 2024 season and has just one career 100-yard receiving game across 73 regular-season contests. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet who clearly busts far more than he hits.

injury.comment: Helm caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
injury.longComment: The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and was unable to get anything going against arguably the league's worst defense Sunday. Helm has been held below 30 receiving yards in nine of 10 games this season. He's nothing more than a low-end TE2 in fantasy.

injury.comment: Mims caught one of two targets for 36 yards and also added an 11-yard rush and 22 yards as a punt returner during Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
injury.longComment: Mims reeled in just one pass for the second straight game, but his 36-yard snag in the second quarter was enough to notch his second highest receiving yardage total in a contest this year. The wideout played just 15 snaps on offense, which ranked fifth at his position behind Courtland Sutton (49), Pat Bryant (40), Jaylen Waddle (39) and Troy Franklin (24) for Denver in Week 11. Mims will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of Friday's matchup with the Steelers.

injury.comment: Allen caught two of four targets for 41 yards during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals.
injury.longComment: Allen was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after having done so only twice in the team's first eight games of the year. The wide receiver played 16 offensive snaps which ranked sixth at his position behind Xavier Worthy (47), Rashee Rice (32), Jalen Royals (24), Andrew Armstrong (20) and Josh Downs (17). As a result of the depth of the WR room in Kansas City, Allen will remain a hard fantasy option to trust Thursday versus the Bills.

injury.comment: Fehoko caught one of five targets for a two-yard touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injury.longComment: The wideout led his position group by playing 52 of 56 offensive snaps, and he ran a team-high 34 routes on Josh Johnson's 37 dropbacks. It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows something more in the box score.

injury.comment: Bateman recorded two catches for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The wideout's big play was a 52-yard touchdown strike from Jacoby Brissett in the first quarter. It was Bateman's first score since Week 2, and his 67 yards were his second-most in a game this season. Bateman has three or fewer catches in six straight contests and isn't someone to chase in fantasy ahead of next Sunday's date with the Texans.

injury.comment: Dulcich caught two of seven targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: Dulcich finished second on the team in targets behind wide receiver Caleb Douglas (10), but he failed to exceed 20 receiving yards for the third straight week. The tight end hasn't scored a touchdown this season, and his next chance will come in Week 12 against the Jets.

injury.comment: TeSlaa failed to catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers.
injury.longComment: TeSlaa went without a reception for the second time in four weeks, and he has now gone six straight games without exceeding 20 receiving yards. The wide receiver played 23 snaps on offense, ranking third at his position behind Amon-Ra St. Brown (46) and Jameson Williams (45). TeSlaa will continue to be an unreliable fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 12 matchup with the Bears on Thursday.

injury.comment: Armstrong caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
injury.longComment: The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

injury.comment: Nailor caught one of five targets for 16 yards during Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos.
injury.longComment: Nailor caught one pass for the second straight week, and he has exceeded 20 receiving yards only one time since Week 1. The wide receiver was unable to capitalize on the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle) in Week 11, and Nailor figures to remain an unattractive fantasy option in Week 12 against the Browns.

injury.comment: Duvernay logged 81 kick return yards in the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Duvernay played two offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver took a step back after three targets in Week 10, leaving the Week 11 wide receiver action to Simi Fehoko and Harrison Wallace.

injury.comment: Spann-Ford caught both of his targets for five yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
injury.longComment: With Jake Ferguson (knee) still sidelined, Spann-Ford played 44 of 65 offensive snaps against Tennessee and ran 17 routes on Day Prescott's 36 dropbacks. The Cowboys don't throw to their tight ends often and funnel most targets through CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but Spann-Ford did catch a two-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter. He has 18 catches for 161 yards and the one score on 26 targets across 11 games this season.

injury.comment: Taylor caught two passes for 25 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
injury.longComment: The Jets controlled this game from start to finish and never trailed, so Geno Smith attempted just 21 passes to 37 run plays for New York. Taylor's 25 yards were his most in a game since Week 7, and he's totaled just 10 catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns over his last four contests. He's a very risky play as a fantasy tight end.

injury.longComment: Shavers played 27 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams in his return to the field Sunday. The wide receiver has finally started to mix into the offense after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in the Bills' 27-24 win over the Jaguars in the 2025 AFC wild-card round.

Thomas brought in two of three targets for 56 yards and added a 30-yard carry during the Bears' 21-13 win over the Saints on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Thomas was cleared to play Sunday after working through an ankle issue that prevented him from practicing Friday. The ankle didn't appear to bother him, as he turned his first touch of the game into a 30-yard rush midway through the second quarter before connecting with Caleb Williams on passes for 40 and 16 yards in the third and fourth, respectively. It was the rookie third-round wideout's best performance of the season, and while Chicago boasts talented pass catchers like Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, Thomas' big-play potential could be something that the Bears lean into for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (233.1) and 29th in passing touchdowns allowed (21).

injury.longComment: Turpin went without a catch for the fourth time this season, but he was able to make his mark as a rusher in Week 11. The wideout was able to break loose for a 22-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, notching his second score on the ground this season. Turpin has now caught five of 11 targets for 49 yards, rushed five times for 60 yards and two touchdowns, and added 695 kick-return yards and 121 yards as a punt returner over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.

injury.longComment: Humphrey will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Steelers on Black Friday, although Humphrey is unlikely to see the field unless a wide receiver ahead of him on the depth chart is not available.

Restrepo played 11 of his 13 snaps on pass plays in the slot, where Robinson operated prior to his injury, but it was actually Dike and Daniel Bellinger who saw the biggest boosts in slot rate with Robinson out.

The score was Bech's first since Week 1, and his 88 receiving yards bested his previous season total of 67 yards entering Week 11. The wide receiver appears to have great chemistry with Mendoza, garnering 16 targets over the quarterback's first two career starts.

injury.comment: Thornton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 tilt against Denver.
injury.longComment: Thornton is dealing with a back injury, but he wasn't listed on Las Vegas' practice report during Week 11 prep. As such, it appears the second-year wideout is a healthy scratch Sunday. Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech, Dareke Young and Cody White will make up the Raiders' WR corps.

injury.comment: Young (stinger) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against Denver.
injury.longComment: Young suffered a stinger late in the first half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now in question. In his absence, Cody White is a candidate to see a slight uptick in opportunities on offense with Las Vegas.

injury.comment: Bell caught one of his four targets for eight yards in the Dolphins' 26-9 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Bell saw 34 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver played in 62 percent of the Dolphins' offensive plays but only caught one pass. The team continues to try to involve the third-round rookie, but for one reason or another, he remains out of sync with quarterbacks Malik Willis (abdomen) and Kyle McCord.

injury.comment: Coleman failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
injury.longComment: With Chris Bell (knee) back from his absence, Coleman reverted to WR4 duties for Miami, playing just 12 of 57 offensive snaps. He has no fantasy appeal while Caleb Douglas, Malik Washington and Bell are healthy. injury.comment: Tolbert caught his only target for 17 yards during Sunday's 26-9 loss at Buffalo.

Miami will probably continue to lean primarily on Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell at wide receiver in a Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.

The wide receiver was on the field for 21 offensive snaps, ranking fourth at his position behind Devaughn Vele (64), Chris Olave (62) and Jordyn Tyson (36) in the contest. Lance will continue to be primarily a special-teams asset for New Orleans moving forward, making him an unattractive option for fantasy managers.

Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
injury.longComment: Shepard was brought up to the active roster for Sunday's game against the Chargers due to the absences of both Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs), and Shepard answered the call by hauling in both of his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in a 27-24 win for the Jets. injury.longComment: Jones' 32 snaps on offense during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs were ahead of both Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (two each) and behind Simi Fehoko (52) and Harrison Wallace (36). Jones finished the game with a one-yard carry and a 17-yard catch on two targets, and that reception ended up being the second-longest offensive play for the Cardinals. Given his usage in Week 11, Jones stands a good chance of being brought up for Week 12 against the Commanders on Nov. 29, although his next elevation from the practice squad is the last one he is eligible for this season.

injury.comment: Wallace finished Sunday's loss to Kansas City with four catches for 57 yards on seven targets.
injury.longComment: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie emerged with a 4-57-0 line on seven targets against the Chiefs, with the targets, receptions and yards all pacing Arizona wideouts. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production moving forward.

Wetjen (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
injury.longComment: Wetjen has operated as the Steelers' top returner on both kickoffs and punts this season. However, with Roman Wilson back from injured reserve and Max Hurleman elevated from the practice squad to the active roster, Wetjen will be a healthy scratch Sunday for the first time this season. Wetjen's next opportunity to play is Friday against the Broncos, although the rookie fourth-rounder's chances of suiting up for that contest would be further diminished if Michael Pittman (foot) is activated from IR before that game.

injury.comment: Lambert-Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
injury.longComment: With Ladd McConkey (back) active, Lambert-Smith will be a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest. Lambert-Smith's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29, although his path to playing time is limited unless there is an injury in front of him on the Chargers' wide receiver depth chart.

injury.longComment: Hurst led the team in targets, and his five catches and 56 receiving yards were new season highs. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.

Walker recorded 211 kickoff-return yards, including an 86-yard touchdown, and one catch for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: The wide receiver took on the role for the first time this season and did well. Walker has seen just 10 targets on offense in 2026, so he's not much of a factor in fantasy leagues at the moment, but he can perhaps find his place on the return team.

injury.comment: Sarratt (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina.
injury.longComment: Sarratt has been active for two games this season, most recently appearing in Week 4 versus the Titans. Since then, he's been held out. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 versus the Texans.

injury.comment: Engram caught six of eight targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
injury.longComment: It was easily Engram's best performance of the season, as he set season highs in targets, catches and yards against Las Vegas. Entering Sunday, Engram had produced just seven grabs for 48 yards total over his previous four games. Engram and the Broncos have a quick turnaround ahead of Friday's date with the Steelers. The tight end will be a low-floor fantasy option for that one.

injury.comment: Njoku caught two of four passes for 28 yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Njoku briefly left Sunday's contest after injuring his shoulder at the end of a 13-yard catch in the first quarter. The veteran tight end was cleared to return, and he ended up finishing second on the Chargers in targets behind Ladd McConkey (eight), on a day that saw Justin Herbert complete 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns. Njoku and the Chargers will stay home for Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

injury.comment: Tremble caught one pass for 18 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
injury.longComment: The tight end played on 82 percent of the offensive snaps but only saw one target. Tremble has 36 targets across 10 appearances this season, recording 26 catches for 245 yards and three scores.

injury.comment: Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
injury.longComment: Sadiq finished tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and running back Breece Hall behind wideout Garrett Wilson (five). The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for just the second time since catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a score in Week 3 against the Lions. Sadiq has now caught 25 of 36 targets for 268 yards and a score while adding a three-yard rushing touchdown over the first 11 regular-season contests of his career.

injury.comment: Knox caught two of three targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
injury.longComment: Knox was the top available TE for the Bills in the absence of Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle). The added opportunities helped Knox post his second-highest total of the season in receiving yards, but Knox remains off the radar in most fantasy formats heading into Thursday's game against the Chiefs. He hasn't scored since Week 2 while recording a meager 117 yards on 16 catches through 10 games.

injury.comment: Fant caught two of his five targets for 19 yards in the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Fant played 49 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The starting tight end was on the field for 69 percent of the team's offensive plays but remains off the same page with quarterback Tyler Shough. The tight end's five targets are the most attention he has seen since Week 1 against the Lions.

injury.comment: Gray (ribs) was deemed a non-participant in Monday's practice walkthrough.
injury.longComment: Kansas City didn't actually practice Monday, but Gray's DNP tag is nonetheless concerning with the club set to next take the field Thursday versus Buffalo. Gray was injured late in Sunday's win over Arizona and didn't re-enter the contest. If the veteran tight end isn't able to suit up against the Bills, Jake Briningstool could see more work on offense as Travis Kelce's backup.

injury.comment: Kolar brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Kolar was cleared to play Sunday after progressing through the league's concussion protocol, and his 30 offensive snaps were ahead of fellow tight ends David Njoku (25) and Oronde Gadsden (23). However, Kolar's eight-yard catch midway through the first quarter was the only pass that the fifth-year pro saw from Justin Herbert, although no Chargers pass catcher saw more than five targets other then Ladd McConkey (eight). Kolar has a 16-153-0 receiving line on 24 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

injury.comment: Higgins caught his lone target for four yards during the Cardinal' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
injury.longComment: The Cardinals offense struggled Sunday with Josh Johnson as the starter in the absence of Carson Beck (back). Of Johnson's 31 pass attempts, 26 of them were split between Trey McBride (14), Harrison Wallace (seven) and Simi Fehoko (five), leaving very little for Higgins and the other Cardinals pass catchers. Higgins has only one catch over his last two outings and a 19-166-1 receiving line on 21 targets through 11 regular-season games.

injury.comment: Boerkircher didn't draw a target while playing 22 of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: Though quarterback Trevor Lawrence dropped back a season-high 50 times on the day and targeted nine different players, Boerkircher wasn't able to earn a look in the passing game. The second-round rookie out of Texas A&M is regarded mainly as a run-blocking specialist, but he had carved out a minor role in the passing attack with at least one reception in each of Jacksonville's previous six contests.

injury.comment: Bellinger made one catch for five yards in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Bellinger played 26 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. The tight end made the most of his singular target but was primarily utilized as a blocker in the blowout loss.

injury.comment: Hawes (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
injury.longComment: Hawes was in danger of missing this contest due to a shoulder issue, though he will avoid his first absence of the 2026 campaign Sunday versus Miami. With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) sidelined in Week 11, Hawes will have an opportunity to get more involved than usual behind Dawson Knox.

injury.comment: Latu recorded a 30-yard reception on four targets in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
injury.longComment: With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) inactive, Latu moved a rung up on the ladder at tight end and ended up seeing his most extensive playing time on offense of the season, logging 28 of 78 snaps (36 percent). He parlayed the elevated snaps into a season-high target count, but Latu's lone reception actually came on special teams, when Tommy Doman faked a punt and connected with the 24-year-old deep down the field for a fourth-down conversion. Latu will likely see his opportunities take a hit if Kincaid makes it back for a Thursday matchup with the Chiefs in Week 12.

injury.comment: Roush brought in his lone target for 19 yards during Chicago's 21-13 win over New Orleans on Sunday.
injury.longComment: The rookie third-rounder connected with Caleb Williams on a 19-yard pass midway through the first quarter, although Roush didn't see another target the rest of the way. With Cole Kmet (knee, IR) out for the rest of the year, Roush will continue to serve as the Bears' TE2 behind Colston Loveland. The Bears will be on the road for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks dead last in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.

injury.comment: Carlson played 15 of his 19 snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Saints.
injury.longComment: Though he's been active for each of the Bears' last three games in the wake of Cole Kmet's season-ending knee injury, Carlson remains well behind Colston Loveland and Sam Roush in the pecking order at tight end. Carlson has yet to draw a target and has now played more snaps on special teams than offense in the past two contests.

injury.longComment: With Jake Ferguson (knee) remaining out for Dallas, Schoonmaker played 25 of 65 offensive snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford. Schoonmaker ran 12 routes, five fewer than Spann-Ford, and the duo combined to see three targets on a day Dak Prescott attempted 33 passes. Schoonmaker has five catches for 48 yards on six targets across nine games this season and has no fantasy appeal.

injury.comment: Mitchell recorded two receptions for 40 yards on two targets in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
injury.longComment: The fifth-year tight end was one of eight pass catchers that quarterback Dak Prescott connected with on the afternoon, with the pair of receptions marking Mitchell's first two grabs of the season. Mitchell took the field for 15 of the Cowboys' 65 snaps on offense, but he could wind up seeing most of his playing time on special teams once top tight end Jake Ferguson is cleared to return from the knee injury that has sidelined him for the past two games.

injury.comment: Knee - ACL + MCL
Trautman caught his only target for a one-yard touchdown during Sunday's 38-24 win versus the Raiders.
injury.longComment: Trautman leaked open behind Las Vegas' defense on a play-action pass from the goal line early in the second quarter, giving Denver a 10-0 lead. He still has a big role in the Broncos' offense, but he isn't running enough routes to sustain pass-catching production worth fantasy consideration in most formats.

injury.comment: Adkins recorded a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
injury.longComment: Adkins was on the field for 30 of the Broncos' 73 snaps on offense, with his 41 percent share representing a season-high mark. The fourth-year tight end out of South Carolina has mainly served as a blocking specialist for Denver, having thus far been limited to a 7-47-3 receiving line on nine targets to go with a six-yard carry through 10 appearances on the season.

injury.comment: Lohner (foot) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
injury.longComment: The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.

injury.comment: Wright caught both of two targets for 42 yards during Sunday's 31-21 win versus the Buccaneers.
injury.longComment: One of Wright's two grabs in Week 11 was a 27-yard strike up the seam, easily his longest reception of the season thus far. He was on the field for 43 of the Lions' 58 offensive snaps Sunday, but he spent a substantial majority of those on blocking assignments for tailback Jahmyr Gibbs and company. His role in a Thanksgiving tilt versus the Bears may depend somewhat on the health of running mate Sam Laporta, who was limited during Monday's walkthrough with an ankle issue.

Briningstool caught one of two targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win against the Jets on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of the campaign.

injury.comment: The Chiefs placed Wiley (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
injury.longComment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

injury.comment: Knee
Thomas caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown during the Raiders' 38-24 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
injury.longComment: Thomas had the opportunity to step into the TE2 role behind Michael Mayer on Sunday due to the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps). Thomas' 35 offensive snaps were his most of the season, and he made his lone target from Fernando Mendoza count, with the duo connecting on a 19-yard touchdown pass late in the third quarter to tie the game up at 17-17. Thomas has seven catches on as many targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns through 11 regular-season games, although he would revert to being the No. 3 tight end in Week 12 against the Browns on Nov. 29 if Bowers is cleared to return for that contest.

Johnson caught his only target for 15 yards during Sunday's 23-18 win versus the Jaguars.
injury.longComment: Johnson was third in offensive snaps among Giants tight ends Sunday (14) behind starter Isaiah Likely (49) and veteran Chris Manhertz (19). With that said, Johnson did manage to record at least one catch for the fourth time in his last five games. As long as Likely remains available, though, Johnson will probably remain in a rotational role.

injury.comment: Stowers didn't log any offensive snaps in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
injury.longComment: Dallas Goedert (47 snaps), Johnny Mundt (eight) and Zach Ertz (six) handled tight-end duties for Philly, while Stowers played 20 snaps on special teams. The rookie tight end is miles from fantasy relevance this season.

injury.comment: Long hauled in his lone target for an 11-yard reception in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injury.longComment: Long ranked third among Cardinals tight ends in playing time, logging 23 of 56 offensive snaps while Trey McBride (45 snaps) and Elijah Higgins (32) paced the position group. In his first two contests back in action since being reinstated from injured reserve Nov. 14 following a five-game absence, Long has notched two receptions for 18 yards on three targets.

injury.comment: Quitoriano played all 13 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
injury.longComment: Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense while Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end.

injury.comment: Ankle
Evans caught all five of his targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
injury.longComment: Evans was able to reel in a season-high five passes while notching multiple receptions for the fourth time in five weeks. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the first quarter when he secured a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Bryce Young, registering his first score of the year. Evans has now caught 17 of 20 targets for 191 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests during the 2026 campaign.

injury.comment: Franks played all 21 of his snaps on special teams and was credited with two tackles in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
injury.longComment: Franks has been active for all 10 of the Panthers' games to date, but he's been utilized almost exclusively on special teams. He hasn't logged more than nine snaps on offense in any contest and has yet to draw a target.

injury.comment: Sanders (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Baltimore, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
injury.longComment: Sanders has appeared in just one game this season, which was in Week 9 versus Denver. With Darren Waller (knee) and Tommy Tremble (knee) both active, Sanders will now miss his second consecutive contest. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 versus Tampa Bay.

injury.comment: Koziol went without a target while playing four of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: The rookie fifth-round pick saw his streak of three straight games with a reception come to an end and also had his snap count decline for the fourth week in a row. Koziol ranked fourth in playing time among Jacksonville tight ends, marking the first time since Week 3 that he had played behind Quintin Morris (11 snaps Sunday).

injury.comment: Morris went without a target while logging 11 of the Jaguars' 72 snaps on offense in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
injury.longComment: For the first time since Week 3, Morris earned more playing time on offense than rookie Tanner Koziol (four snaps), who had previously been serving as the Jaguars' No. 3 tight end. Koziol offers more of a pass-catching threat at the position, but Morris is the superior blocker and also has a more integral role on special teams.

injury.comment: Cuevas caught one of three targets for eight yards during Sunday's 35-33 loss at Carolina.
injury.longComment: Cuevas continues to draw targets at an impressive clip, tallying three for his second straight game despite only being on the field for 14 of the Ravens' 61 offensive snaps in Week 11. Barring an injury to starter Mark Andrews or rookie fourth-rounder Matt Hibner, though, his role isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats. Baltimore will take on the Texans in Week 12.

injury.comment: Hibner recorded two catches for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
injury.longComment: Hibner logged 35 of 65 snaps on offense, with his 54 percent share ranking second to only Mark Andrews (62 percent) among Ravens tight ends. The rookie fourth-round pick out of SMU's playing time has held steady between 30 and 60 percent of snaps over his 10 appearances, with Hibner drawing no more than two targets in any of those contests.
